key_insight: Multiple flexible leaflets in a confined channel can collectively rectify symmetric oscillatory motion into a net flow, with strongest transport at high leaflet density and an optimal elastoviscous balance.
engineering_relevance: The results provide design rules for passive flow rectification in microfluidic devices and biologically inspired transport systems where compliant structures interact in viscous regimes.
method: Numerically simulated low-Reynolds-number flow with multiple asymmetric flexible leaflets in a channel.
Used symmetrically oscillating plates instead of pressure-driven flow to isolate the effect of geometry and interactions.
Built an analytical steady-state framework and extended it to time-dependent oscillations for dynamic transport prediction.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports numerical characterization and analytical evaluation of net transport, showing that leaflet density and the elastoviscous number control the rectified flow response.
watch_item: The framework is developed for a confined, low-Reynolds-number setting, so performance and optimality may change in more complex geometries or higher-Re flows.
paper_title: On the rectification of oscillatory flows by flexible leaflets in a confined geometry
